subject: psychology
title: Working Memory Model: Components
welcome_lead: Baddeley and Hitch take STM apart and find slaves and a boss.
meta_desc: A-Level Psychology Working Memory Model: central executive, phonological loop, sketchpad.
final_note: STM is not a single store — it is a workspace with specialists.

concepts.def: Auditory slave system with phonological store + articulatory process.
'Inner ear' — holds speech-based items for 1-2 seconds.
Added 2000 — integrates information across stores with LTM.

walkthroughs.body_html: The central executive is modality-free, has limited capacity, and directs the slave systems. It allocates attention and coordinates tasks. Baddeley (2003) admits it is the least specified component — likely involves the prefrontal cortex.

The phonological loop has a phonological store (passive 'inner ear') and an articulatory process ('inner voice') that rehearses in 1.5-2 second cycles. Word length effect: longer words harder to recall — Baddeley et al. 1975.
The VSS handles visual and spatial info. Logie (1995) split it into visual cache (passive store of form/colour) and inner scribe (active rehearsal of spatial movement). Capacity: about 3-4 objects.
